slides.heading: Your Hook Is Missing 2 Layers
slides.subtitle: Most editors build one hook. The reels that hold attention build three at once.
slides.takeaway: A complete hook runs verbal, visual, and text simultaneously in the first frame.
slides.visual: A smartphone screen showing a short-form video paused at the 0-second mark, with three labeled arrows pointing to different elements of the frame: one to the subject's mouth, one to the background motion, one to a bold text overlay at the top. Deep dark purple background, cinematic mood, purple accent light, high contrast, match the brand guide style.

slides.heading: Verbal Hook: Open a Loop
slides.subtitle: What comes out of your mouth in the first second must force a response or create a question the brain needs answered.
slides.takeaway: Use a bold claim, a contradiction, or a question that would feel painful to leave unanswered.
slides.visual: A close-up of a person's mouth mid-sentence, with speech sound waves radiating outward as a visible graphic overlay, energy and movement conveyed. Deep dark purple background, cinematic mood, purple accent light, high contrast, match the brand guide style.

slides.heading: Visual Hook: Move Before You Speak
slides.subtitle: The eye processes motion before the brain processes words. Your first frame needs something to track.
slides.takeaway: Fast B-roll, a physical gesture, or an unexpected object gives the eye an anchor before your hook even lands.
slides.visual: A film camera viewfinder showing a fast-moving shot of a hand in motion, the frame slightly blurred from kinetic energy, a sense of momentum in the image. Deep dark purple background, cinematic mood, purple accent light, high contrast, match the brand guide style.

slides.heading: Text Hook: Give Them a Reason
slides.subtitle: One overlay before the subject speaks tells the viewer exactly why staying is worth their time.
slides.takeaway: One line. High contrast. Positioned so it is the first thing read before anything else in the frame.
slides.visual: A smartphone screen close-up showing a single bold white text overlay centered on a dark video frame, the text sharp and high contrast, simulating a reel cover card before the video begins. Deep dark purple background, cinematic mood, purple accent light, high contrast, match the brand guide style.

slides.heading: Stack All Three at Once
slides.subtitle: The reels that never drop in the first 2 seconds are almost always running all three hooks simultaneously.
slides.takeaway: Verbal opener plus motion in frame plus one text line. One second. Three locks on the same door.
slides.visual: A video editing timeline interface showing three stacked tracks starting at the same zero point: one audio track with a waveform, one motion graphics track with a text layer, one B-roll video track, all firing simultaneously. Deep dark purple background, cinematic mood, purple accent light, high contrast, match the brand guide style.

slides.heading: Audit Your Next Hook
slides.subtitle: Before your next edit, check: verbal, visual, and text. If one is missing, that is your retention problem.
slides.takeaway: Follow Ananda Paramanick for more editing insights.
